equation_request.abstract: We systematically investigated perfect state transfer between antipodal nodes of discrete time quantum walks on variants of the cycles C4, C6 and C8 for three choices of coin operator. Perfect state transfer was found, in general, to be very rare, only being preserved for a very small number of ways of modifying the cycles. We observed that some of our useful modifications of C4 could be generalised to an arbitrary number of nodes, and present three families of graphs which admit quantum walks with interesting dynamics either in the continuous time walk, or in the discrete time walk for appropriate selections of coin and initial conditions. These dynamics are either periodicity, perfect state transfer, or very high fidelity state transfer. These families are modifications of families known not to exhibit periodicity or perfect state transfer in general. The robustness of the dynamics is tested by varying the initial state, interpolating between structures and by adding decoherence.

specification.problem: Determine whether discrete-time quantum walks on modified cycles C4, C6, C8 (and generalised families) admit perfect state transfer (PST) between antipodal nodes, for three coin choices, and test robustness of periodicity/PST/high-fidelity transfer to initial state, structure interpolation and decoherence.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of a coined discrete-time quantum walk on small graphs (C4, C6, C8 variants); the exact modifications, the three coins and the families are not specified in the abstract, so a generic finite instance is used.

symbols.meaning: One-step discrete-time walk operator, shift times coin
Coin operator (one of three choices, unspecified)
Initial state localised at source node
Fidelity of transfer to the antipodal node at step t

equations.label: Walk operator
equations.description: One step of the coined discrete-time quantum walk.
equations.justification: Standard coined-walk definition; the abstract does not give the explicit form.
assumptions: Specific coin and shift conventions are assumed

equations.label: Fidelity at target
equations.description: Probability of being at antipodal node b at step t; PST means F(t)=1 for some t.
equations.justification: Formalises perfect or high-fidelity state transfer; assumed definition.
assumptions: Fidelity defined as target-node probability summed over coin states

registers.name: coin
registers.size: deg(G) dimensional (2 for a plain cycle, assumed)

registers.name: node
registers.size: N nodes (N=4, 6, 8 for the cycle instances; ceil(log2 N) qubits if encoded)

specification.initial_state: Walker localised at source node a with a fixed coin state, |psi_0> = |a>|c_0>; the coin state is varied in robustness tests.

steps.description: Prepare |psi_0> at source node a with chosen coin state.
Apply coin C on the coin register, then the shift S along graph arcs (one application of U), repeated t times.
Evaluate target-node probability at the antipodal node b after each step to detect PST (F=1) or high fidelity.

specification.measurement: After t steps, measure the node register in the position basis (tracing out coin); the estimated frequency of outcome b over repeated runs estimates F(t). PST corresponds to F(t)=1 at some t. Repeat for t=0..T, for each coin and initial coin state.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Scan F(t) over t to find the first time with F≈1 (PST) or the maximum (high fidelity), and check periodicity by returning to F at the source. Compare across coins, initial states, structure interpolation parameters and decoherence strengths to assess robustness.
assumptions: Generic coined walk on a finite graph stands in for unspecified modified cycles.
Coin dimension equals vertex degree (plain cycle: 2).
Position-basis measurement of the node register is assumed; the abstract does not describe the measurement.
missing_information: Exact modifications, coins and families are not in the abstract.
